Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Surfing Pelican</title>
<style>
  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #8fc7e8; }
  canvas { display: block; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<script type="module" src="main.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Surfing Pelican

A non-interactive Three.js animation of a pelican riding a rolling ocean swell on a surfboard.

- `index.html` – entry point, loads `main.js` as an ES module.
- `main.js` – the whole scene: a CPU-animated ocean mesh (peaked swell + chop, with foam coloured
  crests), a procedurally built pelican (S-curved neck, pouched beak, balancing wings), a surfboard
  that follows the wave face and carves up and down it, spray particles, sky dome, clouds, distant
  gulls and a slowly orbiting follow camera.

Everything is generated in code; no external assets. Run with any static server after `npm install`
(or bundle with esbuild: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm`).
EOF

I've built the surfing pelican page (`index.html`, `main.js`, `README.md`, with `three` installed through npm). It bundles cleanly with the esbuild command you gave. I also rendered it in headless Chrome and checked screenshots: it draws correctly and the pelican, board, spray and waves all look right.

- **Ocean:** a large wave rolls forward with smaller ripples on top. The water is deep blue in the troughs and turquoise higher up, with white foam along the crest and broken whitewater trailing behind it. The surface follows the pelican, so the ride never runs out of sea.
- **Pelican:** built entirely from shapes in code: white body, curved neck, a small yellow crest, eyes, and a long orange beak with a pink throat pouch. Its wings are held out for balance with black feather tips. It crouches and bobs, leans into each turn, flaps gently, and looks around.
- **Surfboard:** yellow with red stripes and a fin. It sits on the wave and tilts with it, carving up and down the front of the wave as it travels along it. Spray flies off the back edge and falls back into the water.
- **Surroundings:** a gradient sky with a glowing sun, puffy clouds, distant gulls flapping, and fog on the horizon. Sunlight casts the pelican's shadow onto the board and water.
- **Camera:** it follows from in front of the wave and slowly swings between side-on and three-quarter views.

There are no external assets. The only generated image is the soft dot used for spray drops, drawn in code. The page makes no network requests and doesn't use storage.

The wave behind the board reads more as a pale ridge than as a tall wall. That's because the camera sits low and to the side to keep the pelican in frame.
